column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|02-05|1818|Κάρολος ΙΓ'|Charles XIII|Charles XIII was king of Sweden from 1809 and of Norway from 1814. Because he had no children, he adopted the French marshal Jean Bernadotte, who succeeded him as Charles XIV John. He died in 1818.

bio|01-25|1882|Βιρτζίνια Γουλφ|Virginia Woolf|Virginia Woolf was an English writer and one of the most important figures of modernism. She wrote novels such as "Mrs Dalloway" and "To the Lighthouse" and the essay "A Room of One's Own". She took her own life in 1941.

bio|01-25|1938|Βλαντίμιρ Βισότσκι|Vladimir Vysotsky|Vladimir Vysotsky was a Russian actor of the theatre and cinema, a singer-songwriter and a poet. His songs, with lyrics about the everyday life of ordinary people, were very popular in the Soviet Union. He died in 1980 at the age of 42.

bio|01-25|1978|Βολοντίμιρ Ζελένσκι|Volodymyr Zelensky|Volodymyr Zelensky was born in Ukraine. He was an actor and comedian and played a president in the television series "Servant of the People". In 2019 he was elected president of Ukraine, and he has led the country since the Russian invasion of 2022.

bio|01-25|1990|Άβα Γκάρντνερ|Ava Gardner|Ava Gardner was an American Hollywood actress. She became known for films such as "The Killers" and "Mogambo", for which she was nominated for an Oscar. She was also married to Frank Sinatra. She died in London.

bio|01-25|2005|Φίλιπ Τζόνσον|Philip Johnson|Philip Johnson was an American architect. He designed the Glass House in New Canaan and many skyscrapers. In 1979 he became the first person to be honoured with the Pritzker Prize. He died in 2005.

bio|01-25|2017|Τζον Χερτ|John Hurt|John Hurt was an English actor. He became known for his roles in "Midnight Express" and "The Elephant Man", for which he was nominated for an Oscar. He also played Ollivander in "Harry Potter".

bio|01-26|1823|Έντουαρντ Τζέννερ|Edward Jenner|Edward Jenner was an English doctor. He discovered that vaccination with cowpox protects against smallpox, and in 1796 he made the first vaccine. He is considered the father of immunology.

bio|01-26|1824|Τεοντόρ Ζερικώ|Theodore Gericault|Theodore Gericault was a French painter of the Romantic movement. He painted "The Raft of the Medusa", a work that caused a sensation in 1819. He died young, at the age of 32, after a fall from a horse.

bio|01-26|1880|Ντάγκλας Μακάρθουρ|Douglas MacArthur|Douglas MacArthur was an American general. He led the American forces in the Pacific during the Second World War and was head of the occupation of Japan. He was dismissed in 1951 by President Truman during the Korean War.

bio|01-26|1918|Νικολάε Τσαουσέσκου|Nicolae Ceausescu|Nicolae Ceausescu was the communist leader of Romania from 1965. He ruled in an authoritarian way and the country fell into great poverty. He was overthrown in 1989 and executed together with his wife, Elena.

bio|01-26|1925|Πωλ Νιούμαν|Paul Newman|Paul Newman was an American actor and director. He appeared in films such as "Cool Hand Luke" and "The Hustler" and won an Oscar for "The Color of Money". He also founded the food company Newman's Own, whose profits go to charity.

bio|01-26|1958|Έλεν ΝτιΤζένερις|Ellen DeGeneres|Ellen DeGeneres is an American actress, comedian and television presenter. She presented the television show "Ellen" and gave her voice to Dory in "Finding Nemo". In 1997 she publicly announced that she is a lesbian.

bio|01-26|1963|Ζοζέ Μουρίνιο|Jose Mourinho|Jose Mourinho was born in Portugal and is a football coach. He won the Champions League with Porto in 2004 and with Inter in 2010, as well as league titles in many countries. He is also known as the "Special One".

bio|01-26|1979|Νέλσον Ροκφέλερ|Nelson Rockefeller|Nelson Rockefeller was an American politician and heir to the Rockefeller family. He was governor of New York for many years and vice president of the United States under President Gerald Ford.

bio|01-26|2020|Κόμπι Μπράιαντ|Kobe Bryant|Kobe Bryant was an American basketball player. He played his whole career for the Los Angeles Lakers and won five NBA championships. He died in a helicopter crash in 2020, together with his daughter.

bio|01-27|661|Αλί ιμπν Αμπού Τάλιμπ|Ali ibn Abi Talib|Ali was a cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad and the fourth caliph. His era was marked by civil war and by the division of Muslims into Sunnis and Shias. He was assassinated in 661 in Kufa.

bio|01-27|1756|Βόλφγκανγκ Αμαντέους Μότσαρτ|Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart|Mozart was born in Salzburg and was a child prodigy. He wrote more than 600 works, among them operas such as "The Marriage of Figaro" and "The Magic Flute", symphonies and the "Requiem". He died in 1791 in Vienna, at the age of 35.

bio|01-27|1832|Λιούις Κάρολ|Lewis Carroll|Lewis Carroll, whose real name was Charles Dodgson, was born in England. He was a mathematician and writer and wrote "Alice's Adventures in Wonderland". His works combine logic and imagination.

bio|01-27|1859|Γουλιέλμος Β΄|Wilhelm II|Wilhelm II was emperor of Germany and king of Prussia from 1888. He dismissed Bismarck and followed an aggressive foreign policy. He was emperor during the First World War and abdicated in 1918.

bio|01-27|1901|Τζουζέπε Βέρντι|Giuseppe Verdi|Giuseppe Verdi was an Italian composer and one of the greatest opera composers. He wrote works such as "Rigoletto", "La Traviata", "Il Trovatore" and "Aida". He died in Milan in 1901.

bio|01-27|1944|Μέιριντ Κόριγκαν|Mairead Corrigan|Mairead Corrigan is an activist from Northern Ireland. After the death of her nieces in a violent incident, she founded the peace movement "Peace People" in 1976 together with Betty Williams, and was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize of 1976.

bio|01-27|1979|Ρόζαμουντ Πάικ|Rosamund Pike|Rosamund Pike is an English actress. She became known for her role as Amy in "Gone Girl", for which she was nominated for an Oscar. She also appeared in "Die Another Day" as Miranda Frost.

bio|01-27|2008|Σουχάρτο|Suharto|Suharto was a general and president of Indonesia from 1967 to 1998. His government brought economic development, but it was authoritarian and corrupt. He resigned in 1998 after mass demonstrations.

bio|01-27|2010|Τζερόμ Ντέιβιντ Σάλιντζερ|J. D. Salinger|J. D. Salinger died in 2010 at the age of ninety-one. He had written "The Catcher in the Rye" and had withdrawn from public life since the 1960s. He lived in New Hampshire.

bio|01-28|814|Καρλομάγνος|Charlemagne|Charlemagne was king of the Franks and from 800 emperor of the Romans, after his coronation by Pope Leo III. He extended his state over much of Western Europe and strengthened education and administration. He died at Aachen.

bio|01-28|1547|Ερρίκος Η΄|Henry VIII|Henry VIII was king of England from 1509. He married six times and, in order to annul his first marriage, he broke away from the Catholic Church and founded the Church of England. He was the father of Mary I, Elizabeth I and Edward VI.

bio|01-28|1853|Χοσέ Μαρτί|Jose Marti|Jose Marti was a Cuban poet, journalist and leader of the struggle for Cuba's independence from Spain. From exile he organised the Cuban Revolutionary Party, and he was killed in battle in 1895. He is regarded as a national hero.

bio|01-28|1873|Κολέτ|Colette|Colette was a French writer. She wrote novels such as "Gigi" and "Cheri", with themes of love and the independence of women. She was also an actress and music-hall performer. She became the first woman president of the Academie Goncourt.

bio|01-28|1912|Τζάκσον Πόλοκ|Jackson Pollock|Jackson Pollock was an American painter and a pioneer of abstract expressionism. He became known for the "dripping" technique, in which he poured paint onto a canvas lying on the floor. He died in a car accident in 1956.

bio|01-28|1939|Ουίλιαμ Μπάτλερ Γέιτς|William Butler Yeats|William Butler Yeats was an Irish poet and playwright. He wrote the poem "The Second Coming" and was a central figure of the Irish literary revival. In 1923 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|01-28|1955|Νικολά Σαρκοζί|Nicolas Sarkozy|Nicolas Sarkozy is a French politician and lawyer. He was minister of the interior and from 2007 to 2012 president of France. He has been convicted by the courts in corruption cases.

bio|01-28|1978|Τζανλουίτζι Μπουφόν|Gianluigi Buffon|Gianluigi Buffon is a former Italian goalkeeper. He played for many years for Juventus and the Italian national team and won the 2006 World Cup. He is regarded as one of the greatest goalkeepers in history.

bio|01-28|1996|Γιόζεφ Μπρόντσκι|Joseph Brodsky|Joseph Brodsky was a Russian poet. He was convicted in the Soviet Union for "parasitism" and in 1972 was exiled to the United States. He wrote poetry and essays, and in 1987 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|01-29|1820|Γεώργιος Γ΄|George III|George III was king of Great Britain and Ireland from 1760. During his reign the independence of the United States and the Napoleonic Wars took place. In his last years he suffered from mental illness and his son replaced him as regent.

bio|01-29|1843|Ουίλλιαμ ΜακΚίνλεϊ|William McKinley|William McKinley was the 25th president of the United States. During his presidency the war with Spain took place in 1898, and the United States acquired the Philippines, Puerto Rico and Guam. He was assassinated in 1901.

bio|01-29|1860|Άντον Τσέχοφ|Anton Chekhov|Anton Chekhov was a Russian doctor, short story writer and playwright. He wrote the plays "The Seagull", "Uncle Vanya", "Three Sisters" and "The Cherry Orchard". He died of tuberculosis in 1904.

bio|01-29|1866|Ρομαίν Ρολάν|Romain Rolland|Romain Rolland was a French writer and musicologist. He wrote the ten-volume novel "Jean-Christophe" and supported pacifism. In 1915 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|01-29|1906|Χριστιανός Θ΄|Christian IX|Christian IX was king of Denmark from 1863 to 1906. He was the father of George I of the Hellenes, of Alexandra, Princess of Wales, and of Empress Maria Feodorovna, and he was called the "father-in-law of Europe".

bio|01-29|1934|Φριτς Χάμπερ|Fritz Haber|Fritz Haber was a German chemist who developed the method of producing ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen, the Haber-Bosch process. In 1918 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. In the First World War he led the use of chemical weapons.

bio|01-29|1954|Όπρα Γουίνφρεϊ|Oprah Winfrey|Oprah Winfrey is an American presenter, actress and businesswoman. Her show "The Oprah Winfrey Show" was broadcast from 1986 to 2011 and became one of the most popular programmes in American television. She is also a philanthropist.

bio|01-29|1963|Ισμαήλ Χανίγια|Ismail Haniyeh|Ismail Haniyeh was a Palestinian politician of Hamas. He served as prime minister of the Palestinian Authority in 2006 and later as head of the political bureau of Hamas. He was assassinated in Tehran in 2024.

bio|01-29|1963|Ρόμπερτ Φροστ|Robert Frost|Robert Frost was an American poet. He wrote poems about the countryside of New England, such as "The Road Not Taken" and "Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening". He won the Pulitzer Prize for Poetry four times.

bio|01-30|1649|Κάρολος Α΄|Charles I|Charles I was king of England and came into conflict with Parliament. The English Civil War brought him to trial in 1649, and he was convicted of treason. He was beheaded in London on 30 January 1649.

bio|01-30|1882|Φραγκλίνος Ρούσβελτ|Franklin D. Roosevelt|Franklin Delano Roosevelt was the 32nd president of the United States and was elected four times. He was president from 1933 to 1945 and implemented the "New Deal" to deal with the Great Depression. He led the country in the Second World War.

bio|01-30|1941|Ντικ Τσέινι|Dick Cheney|Dick Cheney is an American Republican politician. He was secretary of defense under George H. W. Bush and vice president under George W. Bush, from 2001 to 2009.

bio|01-30|1948|Μαχάτμα Γκάντι|Mahatma Gandhi|Mahatma Gandhi was the leader of the movement for India's independence from British rule. He advocated nonviolence and civil disobedience. He was assassinated in New Delhi in 1948 by a nationalist.

bio|01-30|1948|Όρβιλ Ράιτ|Orville Wright|Orville Wright was an American inventor and aviation pioneer. Together with his brother Wilbur he made the first powered aircraft flight in 1903 at Kitty Hawk in North Carolina. He died in 1948.
bio|01-30|1962|Αμπντάλα Β΄|Abdullah II|Abdullah II has been king of Jordan since 1999, when his father Hussein died. He cooperates with the West and tries to maintain the balance in the Middle East.

bio|01-30|1968|Φίλιππος ΣΤ΄|Felipe VI|Felipe VI has been king of Spain since 2014, when his father Juan Carlos I abdicated. He married Letizia Ortiz and they have two daughters, the heiress Leonor and Sofia. He took part as an athlete in the 1992 Olympic Games.

bio|01-30|1974|Κρίστιαν Μπέιλ|Christian Bale|Christian Bale is a British actor. He became known as Batman in Christopher Nolan's trilogy and won the Oscar for Best Supporting Actor for "The Fighter". He is known for his physical transformations for his roles.

bio|01-30|1991|Τζον Μπαρντίν|John Bardeen|John Bardeen was an American physicist. He contributed to the discovery of the transistor and later to the theory of superconductivity. He is the only person to have won the Nobel Prize in Physics twice, in 1956 and 1972.

bio|01-31|1606|Γκάι Φωκς|Guy Fawkes|Guy Fawkes was an English Catholic conspirator and a member of the Gunpowder Plot of 1605, which planned to blow up Parliament and King James I. He was arrested and executed in 1606. Guy Fawkes Night is celebrated on 5 November.

bio|01-31|1797|Φραντς Σούμπερτ|Franz Schubert|Franz Schubert was an Austrian composer of the Romantic period. He wrote more than 600 songs for voice and piano, such as "The Erlking", as well as symphonies and chamber music. He died young, at the age of 31, and was recognised after his death.

bio|01-31|1923|Νόρμαν Μέιλερ|Norman Mailer|Norman Mailer was an American writer and journalist. He wrote "The Naked and the Dead" about the Second World War and won a Pulitzer Prize for "The Armies of the Night" and for "The Executioner's Song".

bio|01-31|1933|Τζον Γκάλσγουορθυ|John Galsworthy|John Galsworthy was an English writer and playwright. He wrote "The Forsyte Saga", a series of novels about a wealthy family. In 1932 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|01-31|1935|Κενζαμπούρο Όε|Kenzaburo Oe|Kenzaburo Oe was a Japanese writer. He wrote novels such as "A Personal Matter" and "The Game of the Modern Age", many of them inspired by his life with his disabled son. In 1994 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|01-31|1938|Βεατρίκη|Beatrix|Beatrix was queen of the Netherlands from 1980, when her mother Juliana abdicated, until 2013. She abdicated in favour of her son Willem-Alexander, who became the first male king of the country after more than a century.

bio|01-31|1944|Ζαν Ζιρωντού|Jean Giraudoux|Jean Giraudoux was a French writer and diplomat. He wrote plays such as "The Trojan War Will Not Take Place" and "Ondine". He is considered one of the important French playwrights of the twentieth century.

bio|01-31|1981|Τζάστιν Τίμπερλεϊκ|Justin Timberlake|Justin Timberlake is an American singer and actor. He began with the group *NSYNC and continued as a soloist with hits such as "Cry Me a River". He has won many Grammy and Emmy awards.

bio|01-31|2015|Ρίχαρντ φον Βάιτσεκερ|Richard von Weizsacker|Richard von Weizsacker was a German politician of the Christian Democratic Union. He was federal president of Germany from 1984 to 1994 and was known for his 1985 speech in which he called the end of the war a "liberation".

bio|02-01|1851|Μαίρη Σέλλεϋ|Mary Shelley|Mary Shelley was an English writer. At the age of eighteen she wrote "Frankenstein", one of the first works of science fiction. She was the daughter of the feminist Mary Wollstonecraft and the wife of the poet Percy Shelley.

bio|02-01|1894|Τζον Φορντ|John Ford|John Ford was an American film director. He is known for his westerns with John Wayne, such as "Stagecoach", and he won four Academy Awards for directing, among them for "The Grapes of Wrath".

bio|02-01|1901|Κλαρκ Γκέιμπλ|Clark Gable|Clark Gable was an American actor, known as the "King of Hollywood". He won an Oscar for "It Happened One Night" and starred in "Gone with the Wind" as Rhett Butler. He died in 1960.

bio|02-01|1902|Λάνγκστον Χιουζ|Langston Hughes|Langston Hughes was an American poet and writer. He was a key figure of the Harlem Renaissance and wrote about the life and struggles of Black Americans, with poems such as "The Negro Speaks of Rivers".

bio|02-01|1931|Μπορίς Γιέλτσιν|Boris Yeltsin|Boris Yeltsin was the first president of the Russian Federation, from 1991 to 1999. He opposed the 1991 coup that tried to overthrow Gorbachev, and he was president after the dissolution of the Soviet Union. He resigned in 1999.

bio|02-01|1966|Μπάστερ Κίτον|Buster Keaton|Buster Keaton was an American actor and director of silent films. He was known as "the man who never smiled" and performed dangerous stunts himself in his films, such as "The General". He is regarded as one of the greatest screen comedians.

bio|02-01|1976|Βέρνερ Χάιζενμπεργκ|Werner Heisenberg|Werner Heisenberg was a German physicist and one of the founders of quantum mechanics. He formulated the uncertainty principle and in 1932 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. In the Second World War he led the German nuclear energy programme.

bio|02-01|1994|Χάρι Στάιλς|Harry Styles|Harry Styles is an English singer and actor. He became known as a member of One Direction after the television competition "The X Factor", and then pursued a solo career with hits such as "Watermelon Sugar". He also appeared in the film "Dunkirk".

bio|02-01|2012|Βισλάβα Συμπόρσκα|Wislawa Szymborska|Wislawa Szymborska was a Polish poet. Her poetry combines irony with a philosophical outlook. In 1996 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. She died in Krakow.

bio|02-02|1594|Τζιοβάννι Πιερλουίτζι ντα Παλεστρίνα|Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina|Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was an Italian composer of the Renaissance and the most important representative of polyphonic church music. He wrote many masses and motets and was a music master in Rome. The "Missa Papae Marcelli" is his best-known work.

bio|02-02|1882|Τζέιμς Τζόις|James Joyce|James Joyce was born in Dublin. He was a writer who wrote "Ulysses", published in 1922, which describes one day in the life of the inhabitants of Dublin, with parallels to Homer's Odyssey. It is one of the landmark works of modernism.

bio|02-02|1905|Άυν Ραντ|Ayn Rand|Ayn Rand was born in Russia and lived in the United States. She was a writer and philosopher and wrote the novels "The Fountainhead" and "Atlas Shrugged". She developed the philosophy of "Objectivism", which supports individualism and capitalism.

bio|02-02|1907|Ντμίτρι Μεντελέγιεφ|Dmitri Mendeleev|Dmitri Mendeleev was a Russian chemist. In 1869 he published the periodic table of the elements, in which he arranged them by atomic weight, and he predicted the existence of elements that had not yet been discovered.

bio|02-02|1926|Βαλερί Ζισκάρ ντ'Εσταίν|Valery Giscard d'Estaing|Valery Giscard d'Estaing was a French politician. He was president of France from 1974 to 1981. He supported European unification and presided over the convention that drafted a proposed European Constitution. He died in 2020.

bio|02-02|1952|Παρκ Γκουν-χιέ|Park Geun-hye|Park Geun-hye was the first woman president of South Korea, from 2013. She was the daughter of the dictator Park Chung-hee. She was removed from office in 2017 after a corruption scandal and was sentenced to imprisonment.

bio|02-02|1970|Μπέρτραντ Ράσελ|Bertrand Russell|Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher, mathematician and pacifist. Together with Whitehead he wrote "Principia Mathematica". He supported pacifism and in 1950 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|02-02|1977|Σακίρα|Shakira|Shakira was born in Colombia and is a singer and songwriter. She became known internationally with songs such as "Hips Don't Lie" and "Waka Waka", the official song of the 2010 World Cup. She has sold tens of millions of records.

bio|02-02|2014|Φίλιπ Σέιμουρ Χόφμαν|Philip Seymour Hoffman|Philip Seymour Hoffman was an American actor. He won the Oscar for Best Actor for "Capote", in which he played the writer Truman Capote. He died in 2014 from a drug overdose.

bio|02-03|1451|Μουράτ Β΄|Murad II|Murad II was an Ottoman sultan from 1421 to 1451. He strengthened the state and defeated the Crusaders at Varna in 1444. He was the father of Mehmed II the Conqueror, who succeeded him.

bio|02-03|1468|Γουτεμβέργιος|Johannes Gutenberg|Johannes Gutenberg was a German goldsmith and printer from Mainz. Around 1450 he developed printing with movable metal type in Europe. The first major work he printed was the Gutenberg Bible.

bio|02-03|1809|Φέλιξ Μέντελσον|Felix Mendelssohn|Felix Mendelssohn was a German composer of the Romantic period. He wrote "A Midsummer Night's Dream", the "Scottish" and "Italian" Symphonies and a violin concerto. He brought the music of Bach back to the forefront.

bio|02-03|1898|Άλβαρ Άαλτο|Alvar Aalto|Alvar Aalto was a Finnish architect and designer. He is known for his buildings with organic forms and natural materials, such as the Paimio Sanatorium and the Viipuri Library, and for his furniture made of bent wood.

bio|02-03|1909|Σιμόν Βέιλ|Simone Weil|Simone Weil was a French philosopher and mystic. She took part in workers' movements and in the French Resistance, and she wrote about justice and religion. She died young, at the age of 34, in 1943 in England.

bio|02-03|1924|Γούντροου Ουίλσον|Woodrow Wilson|Woodrow Wilson was the 28th president of the United States, from 1913 to 1921. He led the country into the First World War and proposed the "Fourteen Points" for peace. He contributed to the founding of the League of Nations and in 1919 was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|02-03|1947|Πολ Όστερ|Paul Auster|Paul Auster was an American writer. He wrote the "New York Trilogy" and novels such as "Moon Palace". His books were translated into many languages, and he died in 2024.

bio|02-03|1960|Γιοάχιμ Λεβ|Joachim Low|Joachim Low is a German coach. He was an assistant to Jurgen Klinsmann and later coach of the German national team from 2006 to 2021. He led the country to victory in the 2014 World Cup.

bio|02-03|1975|Ουμ Κάλσουμ|Umm Kulthum|Umm Kulthum was an Egyptian singer and actress. She is considered the greatest singer of the Arab world, and her voice was heard throughout the Middle East. Millions of people took part in her funeral.

bio|02-04|211|Σεπτίμιος Σεβήρος|Septimius Severus|Septimius Severus was a Roman emperor from 193 to 211. He was born in North Africa and rose to the throne after a civil war. He strengthened the army and campaigned in Britain, where he died at Eboracum.

bio|02-04|1897|Λούντβιχ Έρχαρντ|Ludwig Erhard|Ludwig Erhard was a German economist and politician of the Christian Democratic Union. As finance minister he was the architect of the "economic miracle" of West Germany, and in 1963 he succeeded Adenauer as chancellor.

bio|02-04|1900|Ζακ Πρεβέρ|Jacques Prevert|Jacques Prevert was a French poet and screenwriter. He wrote the collection "Words" and screenplays for films such as "Children of Paradise". His poem "Autumn Leaves" became a famous song.

bio|02-04|1902|Τσαρλς Λίντμπεργκ|Charles Lindbergh|Charles Lindbergh was an American pilot. In 1927 he made the first nonstop solo flight from New York to Paris in the aircraft "Spirit of St. Louis". He became famous, but he also held controversial views.

bio|02-04|1913|Ρόζα Παρκς|Rosa Parks|Rosa Parks was an African American activist. In 1955 she refused to give up her seat to a white passenger on a bus in Montgomery and was arrested. The incident started the bus boycott and became a symbol of the civil rights movement.

bio|02-04|1928|Χέντρικ Λόρεντς|Hendrik Lorentz|Hendrik Lorentz was a Dutch physicist. He developed the theory of the electron and the Lorentz transformations, which prepared the ground for the theory of relativity. In 1902 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics together with Pieter Zeeman.

bio|02-04|1940|Νικολάι Γιεζόφ|Nikolai Yezhov|Nikolai Yezhov was head of the Soviet secret police, the NKVD, from 1936 to 1938, the period of Stalin's "Great Purge". He was later removed, arrested and executed in 1940.

bio|02-04|1948|Alice Cooper|Alice Cooper|Alice Cooper is an American hard rock singer. He is known for his theatrical concerts with horror sets and for songs such as "School's Out". He is considered a pioneer of "shock rock".

bio|02-04|2006|Μπέττυ Φρίνταν|Betty Friedan|Betty Friedan was an American feminist. Her 1963 book "The Feminine Mystique" questioned the role of women as housewives and started the "second wave" of the feminist movement. She also founded the National Organization for Women.

bio|02-05|1914|Γουίλιαμ Μπάροουζ|William S. Burroughs|William S. Burroughs was an American writer of the Beat Generation. He wrote "Naked Lunch", an experimental novel that draws on his experience with drugs. He was an influential figure in literature and in the counterculture.

bio|02-05|1946|Σαρλότ Ράμπλινγκ|Charlotte Rampling|Charlotte Rampling is an English actress. She became known in films such as "The Night Porter", and she was nominated for an Oscar for "45 Years" in 2015. She has worked with many important directors.

bio|02-05|1984|Κάρλος Τέβες|Carlos Tevez|Carlos Tevez was born in Argentina and is a striker. He played for Boca Juniors, Manchester United, Manchester City and Juventus, and he won an Olympic gold medal with Argentina in 2004.

bio|02-05|1985|Κριστιάνο Ρονάλντο|Cristiano Ronaldo|Cristiano Ronaldo was born in Madeira and is one of the greatest footballers. He played for Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus and won the Ballon d'Or five times. With Portugal he won the European Championship in 2016.

bio|02-05|1992|Νεϊμάρ|Neymar|Neymar is a Brazilian footballer. He started at Santos and played for Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain. He won the Champions League in 2015 with Barcelona and an Olympic gold medal in 2016 with Brazil.

bio|02-05|1993|Τζόζεφ Λ. Μάνκιεβιτς|Joseph L. Mankiewicz|Joseph L. Mankiewicz was an American director and producer. He won four Oscars, two for directing and two for screenwriting, for the films "A Letter to Three Wives" and "All About Eve". He died in 1993.

bio|02-05|1999|Βασίλι Λεόντιεφ|Wassily Leontief|Wassily Leontief was born in Germany and grew up in Russia. He was an economist in the United States and developed the input-output table method. In 1973 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics.
